CITY OF PASADENA
  City Council Minutes
  October 5 2020- 2:00 P.M.
  City Hall Council Chamber

  SPECIAL MEETING
  The virtual meeting was convened pursuant to Executive Order N-29-20 issued by
  Governor Gavin Newsom on March 17, 2020, and was held solely by
  videoconference/teleconference

OPENING:  Mayor Tomek called the special meeting to order at 2:03 p.m. The
  pledge of allegiance was led by Councilmember Wilson.

ROLL CALL:  Mayor Terry T ornek
 Councilmembers:  Vice Mayor Tyron Hampton
  Councilmember Victor Gordo
  Councilmember John J. Kennedy
  Councilmember Steve Madison
  Councilmember Gene Masuda
  Councilmember Margaret McAustin
  Councilmember Andy Wilson

  City Clerk Mark Jomsky

CEREMONIAL MATTERS  Mayor Tomek read a declaration by the City Council condemning
  the September 27, 2020 attack on Armenia by Azerbaijan.

  Mayor Tomek requested that the meeting be adjourned in memory
  of those that have suffered due to death and illness caused by
  COVID-19; and of the innocent victims of the September 27, 2020,
  military aggression between Armenia and Azerbaijan.

  Councilmember Gordo requested that staff send a copy of the
  declaration to the City's sister city of Vanadzor, Armenia and that
  staff contact surrounding municipalities to request they make the
  same declaration. Councilmember Kennedy spoke on the need for
  the world to condemn the actions of the Azerbaijan government
  and stand with the people of Armenia.

  Mayor Tomek announced a proclamation declaring October 2020
  as "Employment of Persons with Disabilities Month," and "National
  Pedestrian Safety Month" in Pasadena.

  Councilmember Kennedy recognize Mr. James Farr as the new
  Chair of the Accessibility and Disability Commission.

  Laura Cornejo, Director of Transportation, acknowledged and
  thanked the Pasadena Complete Streets Coalition for their
  dedication in raising awareness on pedestrian safety; and

Council Minutes  10/05/2020
   presented a PowerPoint presentation on the next steps for the
  Slow Streets Neighborhood Protection Plan.

  Councilmembers Masuda and Gordo spoke on the passing of Tim
  Price, long-time president of the Daisy-Villa Neighborhood
  Association, expressed condolences to friends and family, and
  requested that the meeting be adjourned in his memory.

SPECIAL ITEM - COVID 19  COVID-19 UPDATE FROM CITY MANAGER AND PUBLIC
  HEALTH OFFICER
Vice Mayor Hampton
connected to the meeting at  Dr. Ying Ying Goh, MD, Director of Public Health, reported on the
2:22 p.m.  number of cases and deaths related to the COVID-19 pandemic
  occurring in Pasadena, as well as on a national and worldwide
  scale. She provided information on California's mandate that high
  risk businesses and operators continue outdoor services only, that
  the community proceed with cautious gradual sector openings,
  and provided an update regarding the restarting of in-person
  student instruction; and encouraged the community to get a flu
  vaccination. Dr. Goh expressed deepest sympathies for all
  individuals grieving the loss of loved ones due to COVID-19; and
  responded to questions.

  Councilmember Gordo spoke on the need for staff to consider,
  anticipate, and provide the needed resources to support the re-
  opening of various sectors in the City, ensuring the proper
  implementation of safety protocols and community awareness.

  Vice Mayor Hampton expressed concerns regarding the inequity
  that exists where various sectors of City businesses are allowed
  to operate, but yoga and boutique gyms are still prohibited.

  Councilmember Wilson asked staff to prioritize returning student's
  to in-class learning, especially elementary students; and spoke on
  the need for a communication strategy related to guidance on
  celebrating Halloween.

  Steve Mermell, City Manager, stated that once the City moves to
  the "red tier" of California's Blueprint for a Safer Economy, there
  will be an opportunity for indoor operations of yoga studios and
  gyms; and responded to questions.

  Councilmember Gordo spoke on the need for staff to consider
  what assistance can be provided by the City to address student
  mental health issues when returning to in-class learning, and
  asked that staff reach out to the Los Angeles County Department
  of Mental Health.

  Mayor Tomek shared that he, along with Councilmember Kennedy
  and Vice Mayor Hampton, attended a Pasadena Unified School
  District (PUSD) event, and Eric Shahakian, Assistant
  Superintendent of Student Wellness and Support, provided an
  update on PUSD's student mental health referral program.

Councilmember Madison  GREAT PLATES DELIVERED SENIOR MEAL PROGRAM
joined the meeting at 3: 14  Recommendation: It is recommended that the City Council:
p.m.  (1) Find that this action is exempt under the California
  Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) in accordance with Section
  15061(b)(3) (Common Sense Exemption);
  (2) Appropriate $905,106 from Unappropriated General Fund
  fund balance to the Parks, Recreation and Community Services
  Fiscal Year 2021 Operating Budget to cover Great Plates
  Delivered expenses through October 9, 2020;
  (3) Provide direction to City staff regarding continued
  participation in the Great Plates Delivered program if it is extended
  by the State beyond the current end date of October 9, 2020, at a
  cost of $466,000 per month; and
  (4) Should the Council direct continuation of the program, grant
  the proposed expenditure an exemption from the Competitive
  Selection process pursuant to Pasadena Municipal Code Section
  4.08.049(B), contracts for which the City's best interests are
  served. (Budget Amendment No. 2021-10)

  City Manager Mermell provided introductory comments, and
  Brenda Harvey-Williams, Director of Parks, Recreation, and
  Community Services, presented a PowerPoint on the item, with
  both responding to questions. Matt Hawkesworth, Director of
  Finance, provided information on the staffs expectations related
  to Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA)
  reimbursement for the Great Plates Delivered program, and
  responded to questions.

  Councilmember Gordo expressed frustration with the lack of
  options or alternatives in the staff recommendation to provide
  meals for the 235 individuals that are receiving meals from the
  program. He spoke on the need for staff to provide an analysis on
  how the City can more efficiently and effectively provide meals for
  additional residents.

  Councilmember McAustin stated that she believes the City cannot
  afford to continue with the program; and spoke on the need for
  staff to provide information on alternatives for meal and grocery
  assistance for the participants of the program. She stated that she
  cannot support continuing the program as she believes it is not in
  the City's best interests to use their dwindling financial reserves.

Council Minutes  6  10/05/2020
   Councilmember Madison spoke in favor of the City continuing the
  program, as the City's expenditures will be reimbursed
  approximately 94% from FEMA; and the program has the dual
  benefit of helping both local restaurants and senior citizens. He
  requested that staff provide the financial details for the program.

  Councilmember Wilson stated that the primary objective of the
  program is to keep restaurants open; and expressed
  disappointment on the lack of analysis that might explain the
  benefits this program has had on local restaurants, including
  potential losses to employment and businesses should the
  program be terminated. He asked staff to remain diligent in
  assessing the risk profile in terms of receiving reimbursement from
  FEMA. Councilmember Wilson spoke in favor of the program as a
  stimulus for employment in the City, but recognized the concerns
  regarding the possibility of not being reimbursed by FEMA in a
  timely manner.

  Vice Mayor Hampton spoke in favor of continuing the program as
  it provides meals and positive mental health service to the
  participating senior citizens.

  Councilmember Kennedy expressed concerns that the program is
  not providing the City enough benefits based on the program's
  costs. He asked staff to determine if the program can be minimized
  and still be effective. He spoke in favor of tabling the item so that
  staff may research the participating restaurateurs to determine if
  they will continue to participate in the program, if the program is
  minimized to provide less meals. In addition, he asked staff to
  develop a transitioning element to the program when it ends.

  Councilmember Gordo asked staff to determine if the Los Angeles
  County's Great Plates Delivered Senior Meals program will
  include the City's restaurants, specifically the 22 that participate in
  the City's program, including contacting Supervisor Katheryn
  Barger to advocate on behalf of the City. He spoke in favor of
  continuing the City's program for one month, with staff to return
  with the information requested.

  Mayor Tomek expressed concerns with indefinitely sustaining the
  program given the City's remaining reserve balance, however
  supported the City's continued participation until staff is able to
  provide participants adequate alternative programs or assistance.

  City Clerk Jomsky, reported that 2 letters were received in support
  of extending the Great Plates Delivered Senior Meal program
  were received, distributed to the City Council, posted on-line, and
  made part of the public record from the following individuals:

  Blair Salisbury, representing Restaurant Management Group

Council Minutes  7  10/05/2020
   Robert Shahnazarian, representing NOOR

  In addition, he also read aloud comments in support of extending
  the Great Plates Delivered Senior Meal program, and expressing
  concerns related to the discussion on the item from the following
  individuals:

  Yan Agaev, Pasadena resident
  Erika Foy, Pasadena resident

  Following discussion, it was moved by Councilmember Madison,
  seconded by Vice Mayor Hampton, to approve the staff
  recommendation, amended to continue the Great Plates Delivered
  Senior Meal program beyond October 9, 2020, with staff to monitor
  the reimbursement aspect of the program, and return with
  additional information on the program, as detailed above:

  AYES:  Councilmembers Gordo, Kennedy, Madison,
  Masuda, Wilson, Vice Mayor Hampton, Mayor
  Tomek
  NOES:  Councilmember McAustin
  ABSENT: None
  ABSTAIN: None

  In response to Councilmember Madison's inquiry related to his
  request for an update on the City's park baseball field renovations,
  Brenda Harvey-Williams, Director of Parks, Recreation, and
  Community Services, responded that the renovation schedule for
  various sports fields is available online, provided sports field
  phase implementation information, and stated that she will provide
  additional information in the City Manager's Newsletter.

  Mayor Tomek expressed strong support for the concept of
  allowing underutilized religious properties to be converted to
  affordable housing; and spoke on the need to establish minimal
  standards, asserting that there will not be huge impacts to the
  surrounding neighbors.

  Councilmember McAustin spoke in favor of moving forward with
  amending the City's Zoning Code to allow for housing on the
  property of religious institutions, however expressed concerns
  with too much market-rate housing being allowed.

  Councilmember Masuda spoke on the need for additional input
  from the community on the matter; and expressed concerns with
  market-rate development in neighborhoods.

  Councilmember Gordo expressed concerns with moving forward
  with the matter without sufficient discussion. He stated his
  preference that the Planning Commission, affordable housing
  advocates, and the community be provided with additional
  opportunities for public discussion on the matter in a thoughtful
  process, but with a sense of urgency. He asked staff to include as
  part of any review or analysis, religious institutions, La Salle
  College Preparatory, Maranatha High School, and Assumption of
  the Blessed Virgin Mary School, and others on the interplay for
  potential housing.

  Councilmember Wilson spoke in favor of forwarding the matter to
  the Planning Commission with a sense of urgency to work with
  staff, including a community outreach process, and return to the
  City Council in early 2021 with an updated report on the matter.
